gen-fs-quilon-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Tight, warm, quietly rounded: Pilcrow Rounded packs its tall lowercase close, with curves that never quite shut. Quilon is the one that flexes, swelling gently in its stroke; Pilcrow stays level.
gen-fs-quilon-fs-ranade: Quilon swells and thins in a slow, editorial rhythm. Ranade, spaced wide and shifting only slightly in weight, gives the pair its strongest quality: a headline with presence over text that breathes.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-lisu-bosa: Lisu Bosa is a text serif with tall, sturdy lowercase and counters that spill generously into the space around them. And Quilon above it keeps the editorial tone going with its own gentle swell of stroke.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-savate: Contemporary and clean, Savate gives its rounded o a height close to the capital and leaves every curve open under Quilon's commanding display lines. Pages would move along lightly.
gen-fs-quilon-instrument-sans: Clean and modern, Instrument Sans holds one stroke weight throughout, its c ends pointing apart like pincers beneath Quilon's measured thick and thin. Pages would feel steady and uncluttered.
gen-fs-rajdhani-gf-bhutuka-expanded-one: BhuTuka Expanded One slows the eye to a leisurely walk, all curvy and authoritative. Rajdhani's dense, tightly woven strips make a brisker contrast, so a slightly larger body size would suit it.
gen-fs-rajdhani-newsreader: Authoritative from the first line, Newsreader keeps a restrained gap between stem and connecting stroke, with open jaws on its curves. Rajdhani draws everything like a fixed pen, while Newsreader's modest stress in the curves makes a long read feel refined.
gen-fs-rajdhani-source-serif-4: Dignified and a touch stern, Source Serif 4 tightens its strokes slightly at the tops of curves and leaves a gaping c. And Rajdhani's marker-tip letters sit above it, modern where the serif is letterpress-minded.
gen-fs-ranade-fs-karma: Ranade leads with friendly, widely tracked lowercase that looks bigger than its capitals. Karma, a text serif with a very small gap between x-height and cap height, can go up a size to hold its own.
gen-fs-ranade-gf-graduate: Graduate reads dignified and bookish, with generous white between letters and an unshaded, steady outline. But Ranade is the friendlier one, its mild taper like wire rolled barely flat, while Graduate does its best work holding a line.
